question: Why do some initiates retain faith even without discernment?
premises: Some initiates do not abandon faith in their initiation.
Their faith is supported by scriptural authority.
When discernment is absent, they rely on commonly accepted belief rather than insight.
inference: Faith in initiation may persist through scripture and social acceptance even when it is not grounded in personal discernment.
uncertainties: The syntax is compressed; the contrast between scriptural authority and common repute is interpretive but plausible.
plain_english: They do not abandon faith in that initiation, because it is supported by scripture. Lacking discernment, they hold to it on the basis of common acceptance rather than insight.
